Find My Laser discovery wizard, beginner add/configure docs, safe dummy-profile path; strong guided setup but no persistent beginner-mode toggle.
Project Setup Wizard with explicit Beginner Setup mode, per-step visual examples, leave-defaults fallback; solid onboarding for a young product.
Simple COM/baud connect plus GRBL-config import; praised as easiest free laser tool but sparse onboarding, no guided first-project wizard.
Consumer guided flow: EasySet presets, one-click auto-adjust, AI helpers, camera positioning, step-by-step beginner tutorials; very beginner-friendly.
Purpose-built beginner CNC reference: setup wizard plus Start Carving walkthrough, safe defaults, minimal friction, browser-based no install.
Clean simple UI plus official Hello Contour/V-carve courses; setup via companion Carbide Motion, but no in-app beginner wizard.
Structured job-setup form and getting-started tutorials, but professional CAM with steeper curve, no beginner mode; assumes CNC literacy.

Comprehensive versioned reference site plus single-PDF manual covering every window and feature; the documentation benchmark of the roster.
Structured docs sharing LightBurn's infrastructure; well-organized getting-started/reference/explainers but newer and thinner than LightBurn.
Modest usage guide, FAQ and GitHub wiki; adequate for its narrow sender scope but shallow and infrequently updated.
Extensive per-machine support articles, learning center and academy courses, but no single unified manual; broad yet fragmented.
Well-organized Zendesk support center with task-focused articles; clear beginner coverage but not a deep single reference manual.

Full per-version reference manuals plus in-app video-tutorial browser; comprehensive and precise, rivaling LightBurn.
No learning ecosystem: no in-app tutorials/tour/videos, no forum/Discord; only README how-tos and a GitHub-issues feedback path; self-described young.

Shares LightBurn forum (~501 topics) and YouTube with official videos, but community small and new (GA Feb 2026).
Active Facebook group, GitHub discussions and heavy third-party YouTube as the default free option; no official forum, uneven.

No asset library or marketplace; imports user images and G-code but ships no ready-to-cut content or clip-art.
Integrated Atomm project ecosystem (1000+ free files/templates), one-click open, publish-to-community; strong ready-to-make content, xTool-tied.

CutRocket project-sharing site and free project gallery provide ready-to-cut content, but web-based, not an in-app library.
Bundled free clip-art plus community free projects and the Design & Make store (2000+ models, 185 packs); premium store paid.

No scripting, plugin or API surface; a closed proprietary design+CAM app extended only through Carbide 3D releases.

English-only; no i18n framework/dependency, no language switcher, no string catalog, no RTL; only toLocaleString numeric formatting.

English-only UI; documentation itself suggests using Google Translate for other languages; no native localization.

~11+ UI languages plus Studio v1.5.8 RTL and vertical text; strong localization across major markets.

English-only; community reports the app is not internationalized and no language options are documented.

Free, MIT, public source, zero-install web PWA plus free Windows desktop, no account/telemetry; only free+permissive+actively-developed product in roster.

$99 Core perpetual (3 machines, commercial use); Pro $199 announced; proprietary closed-source; actively developed.

Free download, no purchase, but proprietary closed-source and tied to xTool's hardware ecosystem; actively developed.

wins.claim: KerfDesk is the only free, permissively (MIT) open-source, actively-developed, zero-install, no-account/telemetry product in the roster; the free competitors are dormant (LaserGRBL) or closed and hardware-tied (XCS).

gaps.claim: English-only with no i18n framework at all, versus LightBurn's ~25 localized UIs plus RTL.
No learning ecosystem (no tutorials, videos, forum, or community), only a README and a GitHub-issues feedback path.
Two markdown guides plus a README and three in-app alert help entries, and the guides 404 in the deployed bundle; no reference manual.
No plugin/scripting/API and not even user-savable macros; the whole roster is weak here so the delta vs LightBurn is only -3.
A small bundled offline library and box generator, no marketplace, community content, or cloud sharing.
Device wizard and CNC beginner mode exist, but no first-run onboarding tour, no laser beginner mode, and flagged CNC safety-default divergences.
